findings.detail: launchd/com.vn-market.fleet-push.plist StartInterval=1800 (30 min). Every fire hits the pre-push size-lint gate, aborts, and writes an auto-push-abort signal. Observed today at 04:29:19Z, 05:00:31Z, 05:31:27Z — spacing 31.2 and 30.9 min, matching StartInterval exactly. Compounding cost: 'auto-push-abort' has NO Pipeline-A routing row, and PO is deliberately holding these rows undrained to keep signal-type-coverage-guard honestly red until FIX-SIGNAL-TYPE-ROUTING-GAP-auto-push-abort lands. So the backlog grows ~48 rows/day and cannot be cleared without either (a) landing the size-lint file splits, or (b) landing the routing row. This is a NEW argument for prioritising the three size-lint splits: the block is not static, it is an active signal-spam generator.

The 05:00Z tick filed VN-LUNCH-BREAK-FROZEN-FEED-IS-EXPECTED-NOT-A-DEFECT as INFO, on three byte-identical get_market_snapshot reads at 04:47/05:01/05:16 — all inside the 04:30-06:00Z lunch window. At 05:32Z, still inside that window, get_market_context returned CHANGED per-ticker values (e.g. VIC 213.000 +3.90%, SSI 21.200 +2.17%) and the tool itself reports 'Trading window: VN market OPEN (02:00-08:59 UTC)'. So the feed is NOT uniformly frozen across lunch, and the earlier note over-generalised from a 29-minute sample. Do NOT use that INFO note to dismiss a future staleness finding in this window. What remains true: a plateau inside lunch is not by itself evidence of a defect. What is now false: that a plateau is the EXPECTED state throughout lunch. Needs one clean re-measurement across a full 04:30-06:00Z window before either claim is restated.

get_vn_liquidity_state at 05:30:54Z returns status:'ok' while 5 of 7 sub-blocks carry no data: sjc_gold_gap.sjc_price_mn_vnd=0 AND sjc_gap_mn_vnd=0 (note: 'SJC price absent from DB (no SJC crawler row); gap = 0'), fx_coupling.usd_vnd_buy=0, usd_vnd_sell=0, cny_vnd_rate=0, omo.net_outstanding_bn_vnd=null (blocked_reason 'OMO HTML parse: no add/absorb rows found'), interbank_1w.rate_1w_pct=null (blocked_reason 'dttktt.sbv.gov.vn unreachable from VPS (100% packet loss)'). policy_rates is a DB fallback ('HTML parse failed', is_estimate:true). Any consumer branching on .status gets a green light; any consumer reading sjc_gap_mn_vnd=0 reads 'no gap' where the truth is 'no data'. The blocked_reason strings are present and honest — the numeric fields are the ones that lie. Same class as feedback_nonzero_values_need_plausibility_check.

alert-commander c214 (05:15Z tick) reported get_vn_liquidity_state -> an error payload reading: macro-indicators service unavailable at approx 05:18-05:22Z and correctly logged it as honest-NULL rather than fabricating. Router probe at 05:30:54Z returned status:'ok'; container vn-market-intelligence-mcp-macro-indicators-1 is 'Up 3 weeks (healthy)'. Transient blip vs misreport cannot be distinguished from outside the agent transcript. NOT asserting either. Recorded so a second occurrence can be correlated.

The 05:15Z tick produced the first HIT in several ticks and it pins the mechanism. No cycle-snapshot-05:2x.json exists, so alert-commander's hit on cycle-snapshot-05:17.json can only have resolved inside minute 05:17: file written 05:17:03Z, spawn 05:17:39Z, read within the next ~20s. Tally now 4 hits / 6 misses, every outcome decided purely by seconds-remaining-in-the-minute at the consumer's read. The spec's own 7-minute freshness tolerance (.claude/skills/step-0-cowork/SKILL.md:39, .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md:59) would have made all ten unconditional hits; the exact-minute filename lookup makes that tolerance structurally unreachable. Fix = glob + newest-by-created_at + the EXISTING <=7min check, at both call sites; the <=7min check is what makes the glob safe against the prior-day residue, so the two halves must not ship apart. Secondary: alert-commander c214 annotates the snapshot as '~6min old' — it was ~40s old at read; the age was computed at notebook-write time (05:23:25Z), not read time. Harmless here, but a future reader would wrongly conclude the <=7min window is doing work.
